tools.name: careergenius_keyword_gap
tools.description: Lists the keywords a job posting asks for (named tools, products, credentials, plus any you supply) and which of them the resume shows or does not show. Deterministic, no AI. Not a score and not a prediction of screening or interview outcomes. Without a key: one of the conversation's 10 free keyword

tools.name: careergenius_tailor_resume
tools.description: Rewords the resume summary and job bullets for one posting. Every rewrite is checked against the resume; rewrites with unsupported claims (added tools, numbers, seniority, results or employers) are removed and listed in held_back by reason code. Every result has "outcome": which lines were reworded,

tools.name: careergenius_cover_letter
tools.description: Writes a cover letter (or a short hiring-manager letter) from the resume for one posting. Every sentence is checked against the resume; unsupported sentences are removed and counted by reason. Returns only a letter, never other text. Review before use. Without a key: one of the conversation's 2 free

tools.name: careergenius_render_resume_pdf
tools.description: Lays out a structured resume as a clean, single-column, ATS-readable PDF (real selectable text, embedded fonts, no images, no tables, no clickable links), letter or A4, at most 3 pages. Returns the file as an embedded resource (base64); nothing is stored. No AI: the text is printed exactly as sent.

tools.name: careergenius_render_resume_docx
tools.description: The same resume layout as an editable Word (.docx) file, for a person who wants to change it before sending. Returns the file as an embedded resource (base64); nothing is stored. No AI. Counts one call of the monthly allowance. Without a key: one of the conversation's 10 free keyword/PDF calls.

tools.name: careergenius_tailor_resume_pdf
tools.description: One call: give a job posting (text or a public link) and the person's resume (plain text, a PDF or DOCX file in base64, or structured JSON).
